html:
The Black Power Revolution was a wave of marches and strikes in Trinidad from February to April 1970, driven by anger at foreign and white control of the economy. It ended with a state of emergency and an army mutiny.

Students and unions led crowds of thousands through Port of Spain, and many Indo-Trinidadian workers joined them. When a protester was shot by police, the movement grew. Part of the army mutinied, but the coast guard stayed loyal and the revolt ended.

The government of Eric Williams then bought into foreign firms, especially in oil, and paid more heed to Black ownership. The events echoed the civil rights and Black Power movements in America and the ideas of Marcus Garvey.
sum: The Black Power Revolution was a wave of marches and strikes in Trinidad from February to April 1970, driven by anger at foreign and white control of the economy. It ended with a state of emergency and an army mutiny.
